title: I Don't / He Doesn't
description: Make clear present simple negative statements about routines.
objectives: Make clear present simple negative statements about routines.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to make clear present simple negative statements about routines. The central language is do not and does not plus base verb. It belongs to the practical context of daily life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: do not and does not plus base verb

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the i don't / he doesn't exchange.
This i don't / he doesn't model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you do every day?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the i don't / he doesn't exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I don't work on Sunday.” and “He doesn't drink coffee.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: do not and does not plus base verb.

items: Communicative goal: Make clear present simple negative statements about routines.
Core pattern: do not and does not plus base verb.
Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
